messages:
julia: Heads up: observed handshake failures for internal service mesh when cipher list enforcement changed in canary.
omar: which cipher? we moved to TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 only for lower CPU usage on older CPUs.
priya: logs show 'no shared cipher' between envoy and some older clients in eu-west. sample:
```
[2026-03-21T08:30:01Z] envoy-22 tls: handshake error: no_shared_cipher; peer=service-legacy-eu-west
[2026-03-21T08:30:01Z] envoy-22 tls: selected cipher: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256\n```
julia: seems legacy clients still try AES256 variants. we need to decide compatibility vs hardening.
dave: suggestion: enable cipher preference by server and allow fallback list that includes AES256 for same-family servers (legacy-tagged).
auditbot: created ticket #SEC-2026-430 (tls-ciphers, compatibility) with note: sample failures from 8 hosts in eu-west.
priya: mitigation plan:
- rollback canary for internal-mesh cipher change in eu-west
- add a phased rollout: prefer AES128 by default but allow AES256 for connections to `legacy`-tagged clients via SNI map
- update deploy pipeline to run handshake matrix with legacy client images
omar: rolling back now for eu-west. will coordinate phased rollout next week.
sre_oncall: rolled back. handshake success restored. monitoring.
julia: also flag for docs: when you change cipher policy, update org-internal compat matrix and notify platform teams.
priya: will own the compatibility tests and deploy pipeline change. omar to own rollout schedule.
priya: thanks team — closing after e2e pass. :white_check_mark:
